title: Angle-Angle Similarity Core Test
description: Use two matching angle pairs, triangle angle sums, correspondence, parallel-line angle relationships, and proof critique to establish triangle similarity by AA.

questions.questionText: In a drawing for a ramp model, Triangle J has angles 42 degrees and 68 degrees. Triangle K has angles 68 degrees and 70 degrees. What is the best conclusion?
options: The triangles must be congruent by AA.
The triangles are similar by AA.
The triangles are similar only if all side lengths are equal.
The triangles are not similar because one angle is missing.
questions.correctAnswer: The triangles are similar by AA.
questions.explanation: The third angles are 70 degrees and 42 degrees, so two angle pairs match. That proves similarity by AA.

questions.questionText: During a shadow measurement lab, Triangle J has angles 35 degrees and 85 degrees. Triangle K has angles 35 degrees and 60 degrees. What is the best conclusion?
options: The information does not prove the triangles are similar by AA.
The triangles are similar by AA.
The triangles must be congruent by AA.
The triangles are similar because every pair of triangles has angle sum 180 degrees.
questions.correctAnswer: The information does not prove the triangles are similar by AA.
questions.explanation: The angle sets do not create two matching angle pairs. Triangle angle sums alone do not prove similarity.

questions.questionText: In a map inset problem, A student wants to prove two triangles are similar. The diagram shows a 40 degree angle in each triangle and a 75 degree angle in each triangle. Is that enough for AA similarity?
options: No, AA also requires proportional side lengths.
No, AA can prove congruence but not similarity.
Yes, because every triangle has the same side lengths.
Yes, two angle pairs are known to match.
questions.correctAnswer: Yes, two angle pairs are known to match.
questions.explanation: Two matching angle pairs prove the triangles are similar by AA; proportional sides then follow.

questions.questionText: While comparing two roof supports, A student wants to prove two triangles are similar. The diagram shows only one 62 degree angle in each triangle. Is that enough for AA similarity?

No, because similar triangles cannot have equal angles.

questions.explanation: One matching angle pair is not enough. Many non-similar triangles can share one angle measure.

questions.questionText: In a drawing for a ramp model, Triangle ABC is similar to triangle DEF by AA. Angle A matches angle D, and angle B matches angle E. Which side correspondence follows?

questions.explanation: The order of the matching angles determines the order of corresponding vertices, so the matching sides must connect matching vertices.
